ui_bugs.issue: 'CONCERNS DELIVERED' and 'DOCUMENT ACCEPTED' render in grey rgb(112,112,123) — the Tailwind text-danger / text-signal utility class is being overridden by the .mono-tag { color: var(--text-3) } rule in index.css:177. Because @tailwind utilities is loaded at index.css:3 (top) and .mono-tag is defined later (line 177), the .mono-tag color declaration wins at equal specificity. The user-requested RED tag color for concerns and GREEN/SIGNAL for accept is NOT visible.

verified_features.detail: Both long alt titles wrap at word boundaries across 2 lines. No '...' anywhere in extracted text. Max wrapped line = 117 chars; page media width 595.28pt, 15mm margins. Text extraction shows natural continuation lines ('days with SEO 1:1 migration.', 'post-strategy in 4-6 weeks.') and rest of alt body still renders.
Regression check: pypdf full-text extraction shows 0 occurrences of \u00a7 across 5 pages / 15290 chars.

getComputedStyle(.review-modal-panel).maxWidth === '720px', getBoundingClientRect().width === 720 on 1440px viewport. Padding computed '28px 30px 24px'. Classes 'review-modal-panel card-linear card-linear--solid'. Content dense — concerns text + 3 Bracket suggests + reply composer + timing all fit.
On 640px viewport, width_px = 564 (viewport - horizontal padding), maxWidth still 720px but constrained by width:100%. Padding tightens to '28px 20px 20px' per @media(max-width:640px).
backgroundColor rgba(8,9,10,0.72) (from .card-linear--solid) — dark, matches Bracket theme. No inline white bg.
H3 'Thanks.' computed color rgb(247,247,248) via var(--text) — high contrast on dark bg.

Expected text-danger red (#EF4444) for 'CONCERNS DELIVERED' or text-signal accent for 'DOCUMENT ACCEPTED'; actual rgb(112,112,123) grey from .mono-tag { color: var(--text-3) } overriding Tailwind utilities due to cascade order.

action_items: Fix mono-tag color override in ClientReview.jsx ReviewedState: either (a) inline style color for the tag e.g. style={{color: isAccept ? 'var(--accent)' : 'var(--danger)'}}, (b) use !important on the utility class, or (c) add a nested rule like .card-linear--solid .mono-tag.text-danger { color: var(--danger); } after the .mono-tag definition. Recommended: switch the tag element off .mono-tag and use a bespoke class like .review-status-tag with the desired color baked-in, or move the color declaration into a Tailwind @layer utilities so it wins.
critical_code_review_comments: ClientReview.jsx line 767-771 — Tailwind utility color classes on .mono-tag will be silently ignored anywhere else in the app that combines them. Consider extracting mono-tag base styles into an @layer components rule so utilities remain overridable, or explicitly document that .mono-tag ignores color utilities.

server.py _safe_multi_cell is used consistently for user-content lines now — good defence-in-depth against any future long-string overflow. Consider replacing the remaining plain p.cell(0, 6, ...) calls (if any) with _safe_multi_cell for uniform behaviour.
index.css:1917 mobile @media rule uses max-width:640px (matches Tailwind sm breakpoint) — consistent.

ReviewedState dark background works via translucent rgba(8,9,10,0.72) with backdrop-filter blur; make sure the parent container has a non-black background where this component sits (client review page uses ambient dot grid — verified visually, looks correct).

rca_of_the_issue:
index.css declares @tailwind utilities at line 3, but .mono-tag { color: var(--text-3); } at line 177. Since Tailwind's text-danger/text-signal (color: #EF4444 / var(--accent)) live inside the earlier utilities layer, and both selectors have equal specificity (0,1,0), the later .mono-tag declaration wins. Adding text-danger to a

element therefore has NO effect. Fix requires either changing cascade order, upping specificity, or using inline style.
